name: sqlite_query
description: Run a read-only SQL query over a SQLite database file through Python's sqlite3 module and an authorizer that allows reading only (no write, ATTACH, extension or setting pragma), and return typed rows: an inline page (limit, and a byte ceiling) and, when the result is more, the whole of it as JSON Lines in rows_file. NULL is null, a BLOB is {blob_b64, length, sha256}, text that is not UTF-8 keeps its bytes. The database is opened immutable: a -wal or -shm beside it is inventoried (size, sha256, WAL frames) but NOT applied, so a row committed only in the WAL is missing from the result, which snapshot_status says; a hot rollback journal is said too. To read the state with the WAL applied, run sqlite_snapshot (it copies the set with hashes and has SQLite apply the WAL in the copy) and give its directory or its `database` as db_path: the answer then carries `snapshot` (what it holds, and whether the file queried still matches the receipt's sha256) and snapshot_status says which state the rows are; apply_wal is not a parameter here and asking for it is an error that names sqlite_snapshot. Several statements run one by one. A file that is not SQLite is reported with its first bytes and entropy: high entropy is not identified, and encryption is one explanation among others. It does not recover deleted records or read unallocated pages. earlier_answers says how many other files answer the same question (a different answer is kept as name.2.jsonl, never over the first).

db_path.description: Path to the SQLite database file (the main file; a -wal beside it is reported, not applied), or the directory of a sqlite_snapshot, or the database inside one (its WAL is then applied in that copy).

sql.description: One or more SQL statements: SELECT, WITH, VALUES, EXPLAIN, or a PRAGMA that only reports.

csv.description: Render stdout, the text of the inline page, as CSV with a header (default: the shell's |-separated list without one).

limit.description: Rows in the inline page (default 100, at most 10000); the whole result is in rows_file when it is more.

max_seconds.description: Stop the query after this long (default 25, at most 110); the rows before it are kept and the result says it stopped.

readonly.description: Accepted only as true: this tool never opens a database for writing.
